lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Arlo opened his card statement and counted eleven things he never remembered buying.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Each one was small. None was over sixteen dollars.

lines.speaker: Jo
lines.text: Read them out loud.

lines.speaker: Arlo
lines.text: A film app. A music app. Cloud space. A meal box. I ate that once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: By the end of this evening, he would know the one number he had never seen.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It started on a Tuesday. A film app offered seven days free.

lines.speaker: Arlo
lines.text: Free? Sure. I'll cancel before it renews.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not cancel. After the free week it cost five dollars a month, charged on the same day, every month.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nothing felt different. Money left his account, and he felt nothing at all.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then a Friday. His phone said the storage was full.

lines.speaker: Arlo
lines.text: Twelve dollars for more space? Fine. It's just space.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was easy. One tap, and the problem went away.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A music app came the same way. A meal box came after a long week.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Each yes took less than ten seconds, on a different evening.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The meal box was a Sunday. Four dinners a week, and the first box was half price.

lines.speaker: Arlo
lines.text: Half price? I'll pause it after the first one.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He forgot to pause it. The box renewed on the same date every month, and most months he was out of town.

lines.speaker: Jo
lines.text: Out of town, and still paying for dinners.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That is how an eleventh charge arrives. Not in one big yes. In ten small ones, and a forgotten pause.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Researchers who study spending have a name for what he did not feel. The pain of paying.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Handing over cash stings. A card tap stings less. A charge that repeats on its own barely registers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It does not mean people are foolish. It describes how the sting fades when payment is automatic and small.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Back on the couch, Jo helped him add the lines.

lines.speaker: Jo
lines.text: Five. Fourteen. Twenty-six. Keep going.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninety-one dollars. Every month.

lines.speaker: Arlo
lines.text: Ninety-one? I never spent ninety-one on anything.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Twelve months of it was one thousand, ninety-two dollars.

lines.speaker: Jo
lines.text: Which ones did you use this month?

lines.speaker: Arlo
lines.text: The music app. The cloud space. Maybe the film app. Once.

lines.speaker: Jo
lines.text: If someone asked for ninety-one dollars at once, would you have said yes?

lines.speaker: Arlo
lines.text: No. Not in one go. Never.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That is the trick of small. Nothing was hidden. It was only spread across eleven dates.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three of the eleven. The other eight had been paid for months, each one quietly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He crossed out five that night, and left the rest on his list to think about.

lines.speaker: Arlo
lines.text: It's strange. The charges were never big. It was the adding that hurt.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No single charge ever felt like a decision. Together, they were a year of them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Arlo kept the printed list on the fridge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Which of the eleven would you have kept?
